title: Strong monoidal descent of exact open restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $U$ an arbitrary open. Specify derived categories of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and modules on the over-site of $U$ with morphism universe $w$ [def-pc-derived-category]. On $U.toScheme$ use the standard derived category with morphism universe $u+1$. Let $R$ be the composite of the derived over-site restriction with the derived functor of $Modules.overEquiv(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For the recorded K-flat derived tensor monoidal structures [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], there exists a strong monoidal structure on $R$ (invertible unit and tensor comparisons satisfying naturality, associativity and both unit laws). No internal-Hom comparison or uncurrying equation is asserted.

proof.text: Transport Scheme.Modules.pullbackMonoidal along overFunctorEquiv and restrictFunctorIsoPullback to obtain the ordinary coherent monoidal restriction functor, including its structure-sheaf unit.

Resolve both tensor inputs by K-flat complexes. Restriction preserves K-flatness. Sum the ordinary coherent tensorators over each p+q=n; preservation of coproducts and tensor naturality identify both total differentials. The maps and inverse maps form natural total-complex comparisons.

Use mapDerivedCategoryFactors for restriction and the equivalence separately to descend these comparisons to the specified composite R. Common K-flat resolutions identify any two choices and prove naturality for roofs. Each localization has its own universal factorization, so the morphism universes need not coincide.

The associativity and both unit equations hold on each coproduct inclusion of the total complex because they are the equations of the ordinary coherent monoidal restriction. Equality of these components gives equality of complex maps. Localization preserves equality; naturality transports the equations from K-flat representatives to every object. The structure sheaf in degree zero supplies the invertible unit. Together with the invertible tensor comparisons this gives R.Monoidal, including for the empty open and zero complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_openRestriction_derivedMonoidal (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] :
    let E := (Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let R := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ E
    Nonempty R.Monoidal
